glossary.systematicReview: A study that gathers every study on a question, following a fixed and transparent method.
glossary.metaAnalysis: The statistical part that combines the numbers of several studies into a single result.
glossary.outcome: An outcome is the result measured in participants, for example an intelligence score.
glossary.comparisonGroup: The groups your question compares within each study, for example operated before and after age 5.
glossary.doubleExtraction: Two people copy the numbers of each article without seeing each other's work. The system compares both versions and points out differences, which prevents typing errors.
glossary.studyVsReport: A study is a group of patients. The same group can appear in several articles; that is why articles are grouped under the study, and patients are not counted twice.
glossary.annotation: A marked passage keeps the page and the exact text of the article a number or a decision came from, so anyone can check it later.
glossary.arm: Study group (arm): a set of participants the article describes separately, for example those operated before age 5.
glossary.checks: The system distrusts typed numbers and points out what looks wrong. Fix the value or, if it is right, write a short justification: it is recorded.
glossary.agreement: Shows how often the two extractors typed the same values. Low agreement means the extraction process is worth checking.
glossary.kappa: Cohen's kappa measures agreement beyond what chance alone would give: 1 is full agreement; 0 is what luck would produce. Here it is computed only on category fields (dispersion type, final value or change, higher is better, adjusted), because it was made for categorical answers.
glossary.riskOfBias: Risk of bias is the chance that the way a study was done distorted its result. Each instrument assesses it by domains (for example, confounding or missing data), with questions that help judge each domain.

protocol.intro: The protocol is the review plan. Define the outcomes and the groups to compare here; data extraction uses these definitions.
protocol.confirmDelete: Delete "{{name}}"? It leaves the protocol, but its history stays in the audit log.

doubleExtraction.title: Double extraction
doubleExtraction.on: On: two extractors record the numbers of each study without seeing each other's work.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
outcomes.empty: No outcomes yet. Add the main outcome of your question.
outcomes.name: Outcome name
outcomes.typeHint: Continuous: means and deviations (e.g. IQ). Dichotomous: yes/no (e.g. complication).
outcomes.timepointsHint: Separate with commas. E.g.: 12 months, 5 years

groups.title: Comparison groups
groups.empty: No groups yet. Add the two groups of your question.
groups.label: Group name
groups.ruleHint: E.g.: age at surgery below 5 years. Say what to do if a study uses another cut-off.

studies.intro: Each study is a group of patients. If the same group was published in several articles, they stay together in the same study.
studies.empty: No studies yet. Add or import your list.
studies.label: Study name
studies.labelHint: First author and year, e.g. Ballet 2025
studies.designHint: Used to suggest the risk of bias tool.
studies.addArticleHint: Use it when another article describes the same patients (e.g. longer follow-up).
studies.confirmDelete: Remove the study "{{label}}" and its articles from the review? Its history stays in the audit log.
studies.confirmRemoveArticle: Remove the article "{{title}}" from this study?

merge.title: Merge with another study
merge.hint: If two registered studies are actually the same patients, merge them so nobody is counted twice.
merge.confirm: The articles of "{{other}}" move to "{{study}}", and "{{other}}" leaves the list. Continue?

import.title: Import study list
import.intro: Send the spreadsheet with the studies already selected. Nothing is saved until you review and confirm.

step.mapping: Tell us which column is which

import.mappingHint: We suggested the mapping from the column names. Only the title is required; without a study name, we use the first author and year.
import.errorsIntro: Problems found: {{count}}. These rows will not be imported; fix the spreadsheet and send it again if you want.

import.missing_label: The study name is missing (or authors and year to build one).
import.invalid_year: Invalid year. Use four digits, e.g. 2021.
import.invalid_design: Design not recognized. Use, for example, Retrospective cohort or Case-control.
import.invalid_doi: Invalid DOI. It must start with 10., e.g. 10.1000/xyz.
import.duplicate_label_in_file: This study name appears more than once in the file.
import.duplicate_doi_in_file: This DOI appears more than once in the file.

study.duplicate_label: A study with this name already exists in the project.
study.duplicate_doi: An article with this DOI already exists in the project.

errors.notPdf: This file is not a real PDF, even with the .pdf extension. Send the article's original PDF.
errors.failed: Could not process this PDF. Try sending it again.

search.title: Search the text
search.label: Word or passage
search.noText: This PDF has no text layer (looks scanned), so search does not work on it.

annotations.title: Marked passages
annotations.howTo: Select a passage of the article with the mouse and click "Mark passage". It becomes the source of the numbers you extract.
annotations.selectFirst: First select a passage of the PDF text.

extraction.title: Data extraction
extraction.none: Nobody has started extracting this study yet.
extraction.confirmSubmit: Submit the extraction? Once submitted, it can no longer be changed.
extraction.outdatedForm: The project form changed after you started. Check the fields; when you save, the extraction moves to the new version.
extraction.noPdf: This study has no PDF yet. Attach the article on the study page to extract with the source next to you.
extraction.noTimepoints: This outcome has no time points in the protocol. Ask the admin to add them.
extraction.addArmsFirst: Add the study groups above to record the numbers.

fields.cutoff_used: Cut-off used by the study (e.g. age at surgery)

arms.title: Study groups
arms.hint: Record every group as the article presents them (e.g. < 2, 2–5 and > 5 years) and say which protocol group each one matches. If the study has more than two groups, the system combines them, never by hand.
arms.label: Group name in the article

data.dispersionHint: Check in the article whether the number is SD or SE.
data.dispersionSource: Where the article says the type

errors.notANumber: A value is not a number. Use a comma or a dot for decimals.
errors.notAnInteger: n, events and total must be whole numbers.
errors.dispersionTypeRequired: Choose what the article reports (SD, SE, CI…) before typing the dispersion.
errors.effectIncomplete: To record the effect reported by the article, choose the measure and type the estimate.

extra.show: Other data from the article (adjusted effect, p value, t statistic)
extra.hide: Hide other data from the article
extra.hint: Use it when the article already gives the computed effect (e.g. adjusted OR with 95% CI) or only reports the p value or t statistic. Type it as in the article: the conversion to the analysis scale is done by the system.

alert.arms_exceed_total: The group sizes add up to {{sum}}, more than the study's total n ({{total}}). Check the numbers or justify (e.g. participants counted in more than one group).
alert.mean_outside_scale: The mean {{value}} is outside the scale range ({{min}} to {{max}}). Check the article.
alert.sd_too_large: The SD {{value}} is larger than half the scale range ({{half}}). That is rare: check the value and the scale.
alert.ci_excludes_mean: The 95% CI ({{low}} to {{high}}) does not contain the mean {{mean}}. A CI of the mean always contains it: check the values.
alert.dispersion_unconfirmed: Say where the article states this number is an SD, SE, CI... (e.g. footnote of Table 2). Confusing SD with SE is one of the most common errors.
alert.no_source: These numbers have no origin: enter the page/table or mark the passage in the PDF.
alert.direction_unconfirmed: Confirm the effect direction sentence for "{{outcome}}" ({{timepoint}}).
alert.effect_outside_ci: The reported effect ({{estimate}}) is outside its own CI ({{low}} to {{high}}). Check the values in the article.

direction.title: Effect direction
direction.sentence: In study {{study}}, for "{{outcome}}" ({{timepoint}}), group {{first}} had a mean of {{meanFirst}} and group {{second}} had {{meanSecond}} on the {{scale}} scale,
direction.ifWrong: If the sentence does not match the article, fix the numbers or the scale.
direction.none: The sentence appears once both protocol groups are linked to one arm each and have a mean entered.

pending.intro: Open check alerts in the extractions you can see. Open the extraction to fix or justify them.

consensus.title: Divergences and consensus · {{study}}
consensus.intro: Here you see, field by field, what the two extractors typed. Only numbers and categories count as divergences; formatting-only differences (comma or dot, trailing zeros) do not. Each divergence needs a decision before the consensus is submitted.
consensus.waiting: Waiting for the individual extractions: {{submitted}} of {{needed}} submitted. The comparison appears once both are submitted.
consensus.single: Double extraction is off in this project: the submitted extraction becomes the consensus draft, without comparison.

agreement.title: Agreement between extractors
agreement.percent: {{percent}}% of the compared values are equal ({{agreeing}} of {{items}}).
agreement.kappa: Cohen's kappa on category fields: {{kappa}} ({{items}} fields).
agreement.noKappa: Kappa could not be computed (too few category fields, or all with the same answer).
agreement.unavailable: The statistics service is down: agreement could not be computed now. The divergences below are still valid.

consensus.createHint: The consensus starts from the first extractor's values (filled in with the second's where the first left blanks). Then decide each divergence.
consensus.noDivergences: No divergences: both extractors typed the same numbers and categories.
consensus.textsHint: They do not count as divergences. Check that the consensus kept the best text and edit it if needed.
consensus.reason: Why does the consensus keep another value?

review.intro: Before locking the extraction, check every number that goes into the analysis: its value, where it came from in the article, who extracted it and how it was checked. The extraction locks only when every study has a submitted consensus and no open alert.
review.locked: The extraction is locked: no number can change. To correct something, unlock it with a justification.
review.lockHint: The button becomes available when every study is ready.
review.consensus_draft: The consensus has not been submitted yet.
review.open_alerts: {{count}} open alert(s) in the consensus: fix or justify them.
review.reopen: Reopen the consensus to correct it

check.edited: changed in the consensus, no decision recorded
check.one_extractor: recorded by one extractor only; decided by {{name}}

export.intro: Download the extracted data to use in another program or keep a copy. Numbers are exported as reported by the article, without conversions.

extraction.title: Extracted data
extraction.ready: {{ready}} of {{total}} study(ies) with a submitted consensus.
extraction.missing: {{count}} study(ies) do not have a submitted consensus yet and will be left out of the consensus file:

mode.consensus: Only the consensus (recommended). The list of what is missing goes in the "Read me" sheet.
mode.individual: Each extractor's individual extraction, marked as pre-consensus (not checked yet).

formats.xlsx: Excel (XLSX), with sheets for studies, groups, data and justified alerts
formats.csv: CSV, with the data table only

csv.excel: For Excel in Portuguese (; separator and decimal comma)
csv.r: For R or other programs (, separator and decimal point)

export.acknowledge: I am aware that {{count}} study(ies) will be left out of the file.

formEditor.title: Study characteristics form
formEditor.help: The fields each extractor fills in about the study (country, total n, type of surgery...). Saving creates a new form version; extractions made on the old version show a warning to review. Removing a field does not delete what was already typed.
formEditor.addBack: Removed default fields (click to add them back):
formEditor.label: Field name
formEditor.optionsHint: Separate the options with semicolons (e.g. general; local; sedation)
formEditor.saveHint: Changes only apply after saving. Version {{next}} of the form will be created, and extractions already started will show a warning to review.

errors.label: Give the field a name.
errors.options: A list of options needs at least two options.

rob.intro: Choose the project's risk-of-bias instruments and set which instrument applies to each study. The system suggests and organizes; the judgement always belongs to the reviewers.

tools.title: Project instruments
tools.empty: No instrument enabled yet. An admin can enable one from the catalog below.
tools.textsFilled: Official wording pasted for {{filled}} of {{total}} questions.

catalog.title: Instrument catalog
catalog.hint: The system ships each instrument's structure (domains, number of questions and answer options), not the official wording of the questions, which is copyrighted. If the group has permission, the admin pastes the wording from the official source.
catalog.allEnabled: Every instrument in the catalog is already enabled.

scope.result: assessed per result (outcome and time point)

texts.title: Official wording of the questions
texts.hint: Paste each question exactly as in the instrument's official source, respecting its license. Without wording, the assessment screen shows only the question number and domain.
texts.question: Question {{n}}

generic.title: Domains of the generic instrument
generic.hint: Name each domain and say how many questions it has. Possible answers are Yes, Probably yes, Probably no, No, No information and Not applicable.

study.title: Risk of bias
study.noTools: The project has no risk-of-bias instruments yet.
study.suggested: Suggested by the study design: {{name}}. An admin must confirm it.
study.perResult: This instrument assesses each result separately: choose the outcome and time point.

assessment.title: Risk of bias · {{study}}
assessment.chooseVariant: Choose this domain's variant (it sets the questions):
assessment.noText: The admin has not pasted the official wording of this question yet. See the official instrument.
assessment.whyDisagree: Why do you disagree with the suggestion? (required)
assessment.noSuggestion: Answer the questions to see the suggestion.
assessment.groupRuleHint: This instrument has no official rule for the overall judgement. If the group defines one, the system suggests; without it, the judgement is free.
assessment.ready: Everything is filled in. Check and submit.

judgement.low_except_confounding: Low (except for concerns about uncontrolled confounding)

warning.several_moderate: Several domains are at moderate risk. The official guidance allows a serious overall judgement if the problems add up; the decision is yours.
warning.several_serious: Several domains are at serious risk. The official guidance allows a critical overall judgement if the problems add up; the decision is yours.
warning.several_some_concerns: Several domains raise some concerns. The manual allows a high overall judgement if this substantially lowers confidence in the result; the decision is yours.
warning.several_high: Several domains are at high risk. The official guidance allows a very high overall judgement if the problems add up; the decision is yours.
warning.no_information_needs_judgement: Information is lacking in a domain and nothing indicates serious or critical risk. The manual asks you to confirm this judgement.

missing.justificationOverall: Justify the disagreement in the overall judgement

rule.title: Group rule for the overall judgement
rule.hint: There is no official cut-off for this instrument. Set the rule your group agreed on: cases are checked in order and the first match becomes the suggestion; if none matches, the default level applies. The suggestion never replaces the reviewer’s judgement.
rule.defined: Group rule set: the system suggests the overall judgement.
rule.none: No group rule: the overall judgement is free.
